Otherwise, there would be the impossibility of the *viṣṭāva* [chanting] (12).
Gautama says that one should form eight *sātopagava* and *bārhata* remainders and then perform the conjunction (13),
for it is thus that [the scripture] prescribes [it] due to the deficiency of the *bṛhatī* verses (14).

One should proceed by means of the meters increased by four syllables each: one should make the Gāyatrī on the twenty-fourth day, the Uṣṇih on the first Ābhiplavika day, the Anuṣṭubh on the second, and the Bṛhatī on the others.
However, one should omit [the Bṛhatīs] from the fifth day, for the Pragāthas originate from the Satobṛhatīs.
In that case, having formed a Paṅkti, they should proceed with a Triṣṭubh on the sixth day; or they may go through the sixth month with Jagatīs on the third Svarasāman day.

Having performed the *navasātobārhata* verses as the remainder and two *pragāthas*, they should proceed to the *paṅkti* [metre]; or rather, in place of the last of those, [one should perform it] on the sixth day, and thereafter [the metre] is the *triṣṭubh*, according to Gautama (18).
One should chant with both the *bṛhatī* and the *triṣṭubh*; thus it is to be piled (16).
One should make the *triṣṭubh* on the twenty-fourth day; the *bṛhatī* on the first day of the *ābhiplavika* period (20).
Thus ends the first section of the twenty-ninth chapter in the Drāhyāyaṇa Śrautasūtra. This reversal occurs in every performance;
these are the great points of difference.
Śaucivṛkṣi maintains that the fourfold *prayoga* and the transposition of the *bṛhatī* and *triṣṭubh* meters should occur only in the sixth month;
for he says, "This [sixth month] is like a 'cracking' (*saṃśara*) among the meters," and thus he prescribes them after having introduced them therein.
The teachers, however, maintain that this applies everywhere.
For by employing [the meters] in successive order, increasing by four syllables each time, one places the *bṛhatī* in the middle;
thus he says, "With the *triṣṭubh*, the sixth month.
Because of the exhaustion of the *bṛhatīs*, a reversal [of the order] would not be appropriate in that case.
Śaucivṛkṣi says that the taking of the Bṛhatī cup is for the sake of reaching [the goal];
or rather, it is five months, or nights;
[it is] the Triṣṭubh, according to the more frequent statement.

The *bṛhatī*s are not exhausted; for the remainder consists of the *sātobārhata* [verses], as well as eight *stotrīyā*s of the *bṛhat*, *rathaṃtara*, and *kāleya* [sāmans]. One should transpose the *triṣṭubh*s.
"Taraṇiritsiṣāsati" is the Kāleya; on the day of that [rite], the Abhīvarta [should be used] during the stotriya. "Tvāmiddhi havāmahe" is the Rathantara;
on the day of that [rite], one should perform the stotriya of the Rathantara either in one of the two Svarasāmans.
For another [application] has already been made there for the *rathantara*;
thus the teachers explain.
However, they also study one hundred and twenty *pragāthas*; from those alone he should employ [the verses].
For there is a suspension in the four-hundredth [day], verse 21; in that case, one should likewise perform the *bṛhatī* verses, verse 22;
but one should omit them from the fifth day, verse 23.
Śaucivṛkṣi, however, holds the opposite view, as it is improper [to perform them] otherwise;
for the injunction is that the *stotrīyās* of the Bṛhat, Rathantara, and Kāleya [sāmans] are not performed [in that manner].
Thus ends the second section of the twenty-ninth chapter in the Drāhyāyaṇa Śrauta Sūtra. II.29.2.
However, a remainder of one hundred and twenty [verses] exists. Of these, one should transpose seven [verses] with the Bārhata verses and four [verses] with the Sāman.
The teachers say that one should place the [verses] beginning with the thirty-three together with the twenty-four [verse] sets, and the two Svarasāmans at the end;
for they are heard in the section on the Abhīvarta, and thus it is the Abhīvarta here as well.

However, in the interval between these two, that which was performed according to the *ārṣeya-kalpa* consisting of six *pragāthas* should likewise be used here as well. Among them, wherever there is a symmetrical arrangement (*samaprayoga*) such that *satobṛhatī* verses would occur on each third day, one should employ those [verses] there.
In cases where they do not occur, there should simply be *pragāthas*.
For there is improper conduct (*anācāra*) regarding the *satobṛhatī* verses on any day other than the third day up until the sixth.

Just as one should previously have made the *abhīvarta* the *stotrīya* verses, so too afterwards, in the *indrakratus*, the *brahmasāmans* should be provided with *nidhanas* and consist of those same meters (*tacchandasya*). Even in the absence of those specific meters, others may be used provided they are endowed with melodic chanting (*gīti*) and *nidhanas*.
Thus, while favoring the *indrakratu-pragātha* that has been left aside, one should prescribe the *sāmans* by chanting after it as it is being praised;
or rather, Gautama says, one should not chant them.
The *janitra* [is used] in the *viśvajit*.

Those [stotras] which are in the *pṛṣṭhya* [period] are [performed] in the ten-night *pṛṣṭhya* period. Of these, four are [placed] in the *chandomas*, according to their respective shares or according to the *pṛṣṭha* [stotra].
The *paurumīḍha* is used in the *vrata* [stotra], or the *śyaita*.

The sixth month, together with the Atirātra and Caturviṃśa [days], occurs in the first fortnight (16); the first [month], together with the Vrata and Atirātra, occurs in the latter [fortnight] (17). Regarding the statement "so that these Sāmans do not fall out," the Nihava and Śyāvāśva [Sāmans] should take the place of the two following the Gaurīvita throughout the entire Gavām Ayana (18).
Some say that [the rule] enjoining non-falling-off (*acyavana*) applies without reference to a specific context.
However, the procedure for the *anvaveṣṭi* sacrifice has been established according to the model of the *ārṣeya* (lineage) ritual, as it pertains to the *nihava* of Gaurīvita and Śyāvāśva;
if it were otherwise, there would be no falling-off in the Brāhmaṇa.
Thus, in the twenty-ninth chapter of the Drāhyāyaṇa Śrauta Sūtra, the third section:

"All the officiating priests (ṛtvij) should chant the Mahāvrata hymn together"—this should be understood as a modification specifically for the Udgātṛ priest, for the others are not explicitly mentioned [in this context]. 1-2.
And all the words [of the hymn] are obtained in those very [verses],
because they should praise together due to their connection with the ritual action;
since a sequence is observed, the praising should proceed in regular order.

By the words "The Udgātṛ [should praise] himself with three [verses], beginning with 'udgītha'," he shows that the subsequent praise is performed by the self. (6) The praise at different locations would belong only to the Chandogas; for, having stated that "the Udgātṛ alone should chant the whole," he then prescribes its locations. (7–8)

Having praised with their heads at the *havirdhāna* shed, they proceed hurriedly toward the west; having gone around the south of the *dhiṣṇya* hearths, they sit down behind the *maitrāvaruṇa* hearth. This indicates that for those who praise with their heads, the praise is performed by the others as well.

(9) The *ilānda* should be made the *agniṣṭoma-sāman*; first, in the three preceding verses of the hymn beginning with "tava śravo vayaḥ," the *anugāna* chants are to be performed on the ten-syllable lines.
(10) Thus it occurs in a triplet. (11)
The teachers say there are six verses; the responses (*anugāna*) are performed on the half-verses (12).
Śāṇḍilya says there are twelve verses (13). In that case, one should bring in two other *ṛc*-triplets addressed to Agni: "Come hither, O Agni" and "That Agni I honor" (14).
Vārṣagaṇya says that the fourth *anugāna* consists of three verses (*ṛca*).
For here he utters the *nidhana* formula: "The vow" (*vrata*) occurs; "Svar" occurs; "Śakuna" occurs. And the ritual divisions (*bhakti*) end with the *kalpa*.
"Some recite these [verses] with various melodies; some recite them [thus].

This concludes the fourth section of the twenty-ninth chapter of the *Drāhyāyaṇa-Śrautasūtra*. Regarding the tenth day of both the *Chandoma* and the *Daśāha*: "Some say that the *Agniṣṭoma-sāman* for the tenth day should be the *Trayastrimśa*; the *Sārparājñī* triplet [is used] because of its placement as the tenth. 1.
As for the statement that "the twenty-fourfold [stoma] is according to the majority of the consensus":
the *ṛc*s and *sāmans* are indeed indicated; however, with reference to the entire tenth day, it is enjoined as specifically the twenty-fourfold.
And he would not have stated it otherwise.
And because there is a direct injunction, there is agreement with the majority;

and when the *stoma* is prescribed by a Brāhmaṇa, the application of the *ṛc*s and *sāman*s occurs according to that rule. The months of the *sutyā* sacrifice for those who possess the thirty-fold *stoma* should be observed everywhere.
And at the Kauṇḍapāyināmayaṇa, they should offer the oblations pertaining to the Havis-sacrifices;
at the Tāpaścita, those pertaining to the initiation and Upasad rites;
and at the Dṛtivātavatorayaṇa, they should press [Soma] for two months less one.
"They should be Trivṛt," says Gautama; "they should be Trayastriṃśa," says Dhānañjayya;
"or both should be Triṃśa, according to this Brāhmaṇa."
Likewise, having been initiated on the eighth day of the waxing fortnight, they should perform fifteen initiations.
By this, it is stated regarding the Sarpa-satra:
"The teachers maintain that for the fifteen [days], the Ukthas of the tenth day should end with the Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra; for the Nārmedha has ceased because of the removal of the Ṣoḍaśin."

Just as in the case of the *trivṛt* [stomas], there is the exclusion of the *maukha* [sāman] because of the phrase "from the *uktha*" (17). However, there would be no cessation [of its use] due to the absence of such a statement, as is the case with other *sāmans* (18). Furthermore, the specific statement is the reason why the *nārmedha* [sāman] is not seen in the *aṣoḍaśika* [sacrifices], even though it is frequently observed in those that do not possess the *ṣoḍaśin* cup (19).
Regarding the consideration of its performance:
20. Some say that it should proceed month by month with the *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma];
21. Śāṇḍilya says it should be performed with the *pṛṣṭhya-stoma*.
"By means of the *abhiplava* and the *pṛṣṭhya*," says Śaucivṛkṣi;
"by means of each day of the *pṛṣṭhya*," say Śāṇḍilyāyana and Dhānañjayya;
"by means of the *jyotiṣṭoma*," says Lāmakāyana.
For him, the *rathantara* and the *bṛhat* [sāmans] are the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras], alternating [day by day].
"According to the traditional recension of the *kalpa* of the seers," so says Kṣairakalāmbhi.
Thus ends the first section in the thirtieth chapter of the Drāhyāyaṇa Śrauta Sūtra.
The initiations for the Kauṇḍapāyina sacrifice begin with the full moon day.

Regarding this, Śāṇḍilya says that they should perform the ritual like the Upavasatha at the end of the Upasads and then enter upon the Atirātra; for in this way the procedure is understood. They should offer the Agnihotra for twenty-nine days until the conclusion of the oblations.

Gautama says it should be for exactly one month. However, the ritual of the Upavasatha day should take place before the Soma-pressings, and in this way the procedure for the Atirātra is also included.
Furthermore, there should be no interruption between the Haviryajñas and the Soma-pressings.

Dhānañjayya says that because it is not heard [in the texts], there should be no Atirātra. For, by enjoining [the sacrifice] among other peripheral rites, [the text] does not prescribe it here. They should perform the Upavasatha ritual at the very end of the Upasads; or, after eighteen Śaunāsīrya offerings, they should purchase the King (Soma). In this way, it becomes immediately contiguous with the Soma-pressings.
Śāṇḍilyāyana maintains that an interruption between the consecration (*dīkṣā*) and the preparatory rites (*upasad*) is improper;
for he shows that "they purchase the Soma in the month" occurs immediately after the consecrations (10).
Furthermore, the ritual of the fast-day (*upavasatha*) should indeed follow immediately after the pressings (*sutyā*) (11–12).
Having carried embers from the Āgnīdhrīya fire to the Mārjālīya mound and having cooked the various *sthālīpāka* offerings separately, they should perform the rites of the Pitṛyajña.
Then, they should carry the sacrificial fires further south for the Pitṛyajña;
in the case of the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices, [they should do so] to the south of the Āhavanīya fire.
Whatever rite is to be performed to the south of the Āhavanīya fire, they should perform it in that [place],
provided that the Upavasatha ritual has already been performed; if it has not been performed, they should proceed according to the original model.
During the month of the Agnihotra, the Adhvaryu should offer the food of the consecrated; the others should remain holding on to him from behind.
(16) At the seasonal sacrifices, they should indeed fetch the sacrificial oblations.
(20) The ritual attendance upon the Agnihotra fire, the Viṣṇu-strides, and the Samiṣṭayajus offerings should not be performed. (21)

"And the Avabhṛtha-nyāṅga [rite] as well," says Śāṇḍilyāyana (22). "They should place fuel-sticks there; those [details] have been stated previously" (23). "Everything should be performed," says Dhānañjayya (24).

"One should [sacrifice] for a month with the *darśapūrṇamāsa* sacrifices: the first half of the month with the *āmāvāsya* (new moon) sacrifice and the latter half with the *paurṇamāsa* (full moon) sacrifice.

(25) "The *pitṛyajña* (ancestral sacrifice) should take place once at the *āmāvāsya* [sacrifice], and it need not be performed [separately]," says Gautama. (26) "And it need not be performed even once," says Śāṇḍilya. (27)
"It should be performed day after day," says Dhānañjayya.

(28) Thus ends the second section in the thirtieth chapter of the Drāhyāyaṇa Śrauta Sūtra. [The text] conforms to the Brāhmaṇa statement, "For a month [they sacrifice] with the Sākamedhas. Having sacrificed with the Gṛhamedhīya, they should conclude the remainder of that very [rite] on that same day. (1)
Thus, they are performed thirty times;
however, in the original rite (*prakṛti*), they should be practiced exactly fifteen times, and that constitutes a month.

Regarding the *Agnihotra* and the *Daśahotṛ*: the Adhvaryu priests study the *Daśahotṛ* as the ritual attendance (*upasthāna*) for the *Agnihotra*; the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) intended by the subsequent [verses] are those who utter the *vaṣaṭ* call in the sacrifice.
They should consume [the soma] from cups with handles that resemble bowls.
The combination with the Hotṛ has been stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
The Brahman priest, other than the Hotṛ, should perform the transfer from his own seat.
Likewise, some [hold that] the Udgātṛ, Prastotṛ, and Āgnīdhra [should perform the duties of the Neṣṭṛ],
because of the possibility [of such a rule] arising from the scripture;
for it would have been the case that "he who is the Neṣṭṛ shall be the Udgātṛ."

"Gṛhapati, gṛhapati, Subrahmaṇya"—he shows that these two are not to be compounded. 11. By this, the initiation and other rites for the Tāpaścita have been explained. 12. There follow the deliberations regarding its course. 13.
Dhānañjayya maintains that the Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin should take place every day.
(14) There are four Jyotiṣṭomas; this Abhijit is a five-day rite which should be repeated over six months. (15) The Mahāvrata is the Viṣuvat day. (16)
Then, having turned back by those same [reversals], they proceed for the next six months;
in the place of the Viśvajit and Abhijit [sacrifices],
this is the course of Tatpuruṣa Nārāyaṇa.

This very five-day rite alone [constitutes] the entire year, with the Viśvajit and Abhijit occupying the positions of the month-ends; thus they speak of it as lasting for a lifetime. For the Stotrīyā verses constitute a distribution over a hundred years in summary. Indeed, the Abhijit is a day belonging to Agni.
The Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice has either the Rathantara as its *pṛṣṭha* chant (23) or the Bṛhat as its *pṛṣṭha* chant for Indra (24).
When there is an alternation, the Bṛhat and Rathantara should be used on the sixth day; that [belongs] to Indra and Agni (25).
That is the sacrificial session (ayana) of Indra and Agni (26);
it has the Ubhaya-sāman for Brahman and Prajāpati (27); Vāyu has the Vairūpa-pṛṣṭha or the Vrata-stotra (28).
The Viśvajit [sacrifice] has the Vairāja as its Pṛṣṭha-stotra for Āditya (29);
it has the Śakvarī as its Pṛṣṭha-stotra for the Waters (30); it has the Revatī as its Pṛṣṭha-stotra for Cattle (31).
Of Prajāpati, the Vāmadevya-pṛṣṭha; 32.
Of the Viśvedevas, the Svara-pṛṣṭha; 33.
Of Sūrya, the Mahādivākīrtya-pṛṣṭha; 34.
"Mahendra has the Mahāvrata as its back" (35).
Thus ends the third section in the thirtieth chapter of the Drāhyāyaṇa Śrauta Sūtra.

Regarding the Kṣullakatāpaścita and Mahātāpaścita sacrifices, the periods of initiation, upasad, pressing-day, and the months constitute four distinct sets of four for each year of the subsequent [sacrifice]. 1.
The years of the other [world] are two; the increase and decrease of the months of the solstices are established in the Gavāmayana sacrifice;
[next are] the deliberations on the northern course.
They should undertake the Gavāmayana for four years;
or they may undertake the first three [sacrifices] with the Dṛtivātavatorayana as the fourth;
or there should be the Kausurubindasāyana.
Or by means of the Jyotiṣṭoma; with that [sacrifice], three subsequent [days] [are performed]; for that [sacrifice], the Rathantara and the Bṛhat are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras in alternation.
"By means of the channel of Dṛti and Vātavat," as stated by the Kṣairakalambis according to their own traditional recitation of the *kalpa* and *ārṣeya*;
"the Agniṣṭomas are Trivṛt, and the others are Ukthyas"— in that case, because they are not mentioned, there would be no Atirātras nor Viṣuvants, so says Śāṇḍilya.
Dhānañjayya says that the other [type of sacrifice] follows the rule of the *sattra* (sacrificial session).
There should be two *atirātra*s on both sides;
in the middle is the *viṣuvat*, having the *bṛhat* as its *pṛṣṭha* chant, with the *rathantara* at the midday pressing, and consisting of fifteen and seventeen verses.
It should be performed in each individual year-group (17),
or in the final one among the groups (18),
or separately in each of the years (19).
For them, the Viṣuvat days should be according to their respective stomas.

(20) That which consists of the Trivṛt [stomas] should have the Rathantara as the Pṛṣṭha-stotra and the Bṛhat as the Brahmasāman. (21) In the subsequent [days], it should have the Bṛhat as the Pṛṣṭha-stotra and the Rathantara at the midday pressing. (22)

The conception should take place on a day suitable for sacrifice, during the bright fortnight (pūrvapakṣa) while the half-month has not yet passed; or during the dark fortnight (aparapakṣa) on odd-numbered days.
Regarding the *sahasrasāvya* sacrifice, the teachers say it consists of one thousand days together with two *atirātra* rites, for he says, "It is called the *sahasrasāvya*."
Śaucivṛkṣi says it is "in between. 26.
He prescribes two *atirātra*s in between the thousand great [days]. 27. Its ritual procedure is that of the *ayana*. 28.

An Atirātra, a Trikadruka, three Trirātras, one hundred and sixty-four Abhiplava days, a night, a Vrata, and an Atirātra—thus [is the sequence]. "A Vrata, an Atirātra"—thus [it is stated]. This is the fourth section in the thirtieth chapter of the Drāhyāyaṇa Śrauta Sūtra. 4.
On the southern bank of the Sarasvatī, at Vinaśana, they should undergo initiation for the Sārasvata [Sattra]. 1.
Gautama says that on the sixth day of the waxing fortnight there should be the *atirātra* sacrifice;

thus the *āmāvāsya* sacrifice is performed in its own proper place. Or, according to Dhānaṃjayya, having been initiated on the seventh day, the commencement (*prasava*) should take place on the day of the new moon sacrifice. The subsequent two pressings are for the sake of restoration.
And the new-moon [offering] is performed in its own place; for the first fortnight is indeed the place of the new moon. Before the night, they should perform the evening milking.
When the Atirātra sacrifice has been completed, they should perform the sacrifice with the morning milk (prātardoha) as the Sānnāyya offering.

Having sacrificed with the Sānnāyya, the Adhvaryu, standing facing east at the edge of the Āhavanīya fire, should throw away the wooden pin (śamyā); however, if the sacrifice concludes according to the standard rites, he should throw it away while remaining in his place.
This has been stated by the Brāhmaṇa:
"The chariot-pole (cakrīvattā) [is required],
and likewise there should be the wife's hall (patnīśālā) and the śāmitra fire-altar."
These [materials] should be placed according to their respective locations if the ground is level;
on uneven ground, they should be arranged in successive order.
They should remove the earth from the altar (vedi), as well as from the high-altar (uttaravedi) and the sacrificial hearths (dhiṣṇya).
Having settled them in their respective places, they should offer them.
(17) "The sacrificial post has a mortar-base," thus it should have a broad base.
(18) "Having dragged it," thus they should indeed drag it first without lifting it up. (19)
"It is indeed strewn" means it should remain unstaked, merely covered over with dust.
(20) "They do not dig the *uparavas*"—the *uparavas* are the pits beneath the two pressing-boards; this is a prohibition against them.
(21) They should rather scratch them out; they should not dig them. (22)
"For them, on the full moon day, there is the Goṣṭoma," [it is said]. "It should take place on the day of sacrifice," say the teachers (Ācāryas).
"When the Goṣṭoma has been completed, [there is] the Paurṇamāsa," [he says], for he ordains it at the conclusion of the sacrificial form.
"The moon being filled" and "the moon being diminished"—these are designations for the two fortnights as if they were wholes.

(Sūtra 26) But it should indeed occur on the full-moon day; (Sūtra 27) for he enjoins them directly by saying, "of these [rites] on the full-moon day" and "of these [rites] on the new-moon day. (Sūtra 28)

The *saṃsthā* (concluding rites) of the *darśapūrṇamāsa* sacrifices consist merely of the immediate sequence of the ritual acts. (26) There is a consensus among the authorities regarding the statements, "He [the moon] fills up" and "He wanes," according to how they occur more frequently.
(30) Dhānaṃjayya says that when the *goṣṭoma* sacrifice has concluded, they should depart on that very day after having sacrificed with the *paurṇamāsa* oblation. (31)
"They should remain right there for that night without performing the sacrifice," says Śāṇḍilya;
"having merely prepared themselves," says Gautama; "but they should perform the sacrifice on the following day," says Drāhyāyaṇa.
Thus ends the first section of the thirty-first chapter in the *Drāhyāyaṇa-Śrautasūtra*.

By this, the [procedure for] the *āyus* sacrifice is explained. In that regard, Dhānañjayya says: "On the new moon day, they should have the evening milking performed, and the morning milking before the *prātaranuvāka*.
Śāṇḍilyāyana says: "In this way, the *sānnāyya* remains milked for too long a time."
They should perform one or the other of the two remaining [rites]. For the Kauṇḍapāyina, the eating has been prescribed; in the Iṣṭyayana sacrifices, the rules of the Darśapūrṇamāsa apply as well.
On the festival days (parvan), however, they should be of the measure of the moon.
For that [measure] reaches even the individual [soma-stalks]. At the confluence of the Dṛṣadvatī, they should offer the Aponaptrīya sacrifice if it should have water;
Dhānañjayya says [it should be offered] even if it has no water.
Regarding the rule "they shall offer a bull for every hundred cows," this refers to a hundred heifers that are not pregnant.
They should guard them wherever there is safety for cattle. They may consume [the milk] of those cows along with bulls and clarified butter.

When those [cows] have reached the number of one thousand, having performed the *gavātirātra* sacrifice in the bright fortnight and having given them away, they should rise [from the session]. (13) Since it is said, "when they are deprived of everything," this entitlement belongs to those very [cows], because they constitute the context. (14) In that case, there is the *viśvajit-ati-rātra*. (15)

If the householder dies, [the ritual] may be concluded at the end of the sixteenth day from its commencement; these two calamities may also arise in the dark fortnight. They should not perform the final purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*) in the Sarasvatī river even once, for this river serves as a sacrificial ground (*devayajana*).
When [the water] is no longer present, they should draw it from the side of the Sarasvatī itself;
when they reach Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa, that is the "rising" (utthāna).
They should throw [the vessel] in such a way that they arrive at it during the first fortnight.
